title: Gaussian rotation endpoint in $L^1$
statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $\gamma$ be the standard Gaussian probability measure on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be integrable with respect to $\gamma$. For $(X,Y)$ distributed according to $\gamma\times\gamma$, the $L^1$ norm of
\[
f\bigl(\cos(\arccos\rho)X+\sin(\arccos\rho)Y\bigr)-f(X)
\]
tends to $0$ as $\rho\to1$.
hypotheses_covered: $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ is integrable with respect to $\gamma$
